name: Jarrow Formulas
owner: Vytalogy Wellness, held by the private equity firm New Mountain Capital
history: Jarrow Rogovin founded Jarrow Formulas in Los Angeles in 1977, at first delivering supplement orders in person to local health food stores. The company launched its Jarro-Dophilus probiotic in 1986, and in 2000 a sister company opened a manufacturing, packaging and laboratory site in Santa Fe Springs, California. Rogovin also founded the International Probiotics Association in 2001. The private equity firm New Mountain Capital bought Jarrow Formulas effective 1 September 2020 and acquired Natrol that November. In January 2022 the two were combined under a new parent, Vytalogy Wellness, while keeping their own brand names.

positives.text: ConsumerLab's public brand page reports that of 8 Jarrow Formulas products it selected for testing, 7 were approved for quality and 1 was not.
The company states that raw materials are tested for identity, purity and potency before production and that finished products are tested again in its in-house analytical laboratories.
In 2006 NSF International awarded GMP registration to the Santa Fe Springs manufacturing facility of Jarrow Industries, which the brand describes as its sister company.

negatives.text: In January 2018 Jarrow Formulas recalled 2,853 units of Liquid L-Carnitine nationwide (FDA Class II) after one lot showed a higher-than-normal microbial result at a six-month check.
In December 2005 Jarrow Formulas recalled its Ginkgo biloba 50:1 products because raw material potency was below the label claim, according to ConsumerLab's recall record.
Jarrow Formulas has been private-equity owned since New Mountain Capital bought it in September 2020; founder Jarrow Rogovin stayed on as chairman at the time of the sale.
